A0236.title: Robot Black Box & Behavior Audit
A0236.definition: Ensuring robot physical behavior is traceable and accountable via robot black-box logging of the full perception-decision-action chain, on-chain action-log auditing, explainable decisions, and human-in-the-loop.
A0236.description:
Robot black box & behavior audit addresses the problem of unclear liability and non-traceable decision processes after robot physical-harm accidents, building on the aviation black-box concept. First, robot black box logs the full chain — perception input, model decision, planned trajectory, executed action — during runtime, enabling post-incident decision-process reconstruction. Second, on-chain action-log auditing writes key action logs to a chain or tamper-evident storage, preventing vendors or operators from tampering after the fact. Third, explainable decisions — VLA/LLM decision outputs carry explainable rationales, facilitating accident investigation. Fourth, human-in-the-loop retains human confirmation for high-risk decisions, clarifying human-robot liability boundaries.

This measure is the governance core after liability disputes in incidents like Knightscope K5 collisions and Tesla Autopilot fatalities; it works with A0072 (algorithm audit mechanism), specialized for the physical-behavior traceability of embodied devices, key to EU AI Act high-risk AI obligations and Chinese robot-liability legislation.
A0236.limitation: Full-chain log data volume is large, with high storage and transmission cost; on-chain auditing adds latency, hard to put all actions on-chain in real time; explainable decisions may leak model intellectual property; human-in-the-loop reduces automation, in tension with the autonomy goal of embodied intelligence.
